text.insert: The accepted lifecycle design gives each game one continuing harness worktree and one durable timeline. Epochs, Sync operations, and save points describe progress within that harness; they do not require a cycle to open or close. Runtime migration is pending, so the cycle contract retained below describes the implementation being replaced.
Harness Timeline

The timeline records ordered events for the selected game across pauses, process restarts, epochs, and Sync operations. Each entry has a stable identity, durable ordering, occurrence time, causal event, workflow identity, and applicable run, epoch, Sync, and save-point references. Record previous and accepted source heads for source transitions. Exact new event names and storage fields remain implementation decisions.

rows: Initial Sync accepted
Initialized worktree identity, upstream revision, configuration provenance, and initial save point.
Establishes the first accepted harness head.
Epoch settled
Epoch identity, input head, accepted output head, outcomes, and epoch save point.
Advances the head only when integration accepted source changes.
Sync settled
Sync identity, prior and resulting heads, prior and accepted upstream revisions, source refresh outcomes, and evidence references.
Advances the head only when source reconciliation changes it. A no-change Sync still records completion.
Next epoch admitted
Epoch identity, accepted head, report provenance, and selected knowledge/index versions or watermarks.
Starts work from the accepted post-sync state without moving head.
Pause, failure, or resume
Requested action, settled work, blockers, causal operation, and recovery result.
Does not manufacture a source revision or end the harness.

text.insert: Evidence and Recovery

Epoch evidence measures worker progress before the following Sync. Post-sync evidence measures the reconciled checkout. Attribute these deltas separately so upstream improvements are not reported as worker gains. Compare matching scores only when their target scope, build configuration, and metric definition agree.

The next epoch refreshes report truth and board eligibility against the accepted post-sync head. Historical measurements remain attached to their original revisions; refreshing the baseline does not reset history. Source-stable Sync can reuse verified build evidence when its build inputs are unchanged, while recording separate knowledge refresh outcomes.

Persist a recoverable boundary for accepted head changes and their timeline entries. Git and database writes require recovery coordination; they are not assumed to share one transaction. Retrying a boundary reuses its identity and cannot double-count progress. Record a failure without creating a success event or moving head.

Save-point failure marks evidence stale and blocks admission until repaired. It does not undo already accepted source publication. Resume reconciles durable workflow and worktree state before scheduling new work.
Cycle Responsibility Transfer

rows: Canonical worktree and mutable head
Harness state identifies the maintained worktree and accepted head.
Opening baseline and upstream lineage
Initial save point preserves origin; harness state tracks the latest accepted upstream revision; timeline preserves earlier revisions.
Timeline and workflow links
Harness timeline links durable run, epoch, Sync, and save-point records.
Blockers, process state, and trace grouping
Harness coordination and workflow records preserve pause, recovery, and causation.
Explicit open and close
Initial Sync establishes readiness. Pause and resume replace lifecycle closure; historical cycle records remain readable during migration.

text.insert: Legacy Cycle Contract
The following sections document existing cycle storage and behavior for migration. Their cycle-open, cycle-close, and cycle-worktree requirements do not govern the accepted continuing-harness design.

A cycle is the durable container for one bounded period of work on a game. It fixes the opening baseline, owns the mutable head lineage and ordered workflow evidence, and remains inspectable after an explicit operator close.
CycleState
CycleState extends the
StateEnvelope
with cycle-owned lineage, timeline, child workflow identities, and close state. It never holds the game dispatch lease itself.

props.description: Durable container owning the worktree, head lineage, timeline, and child workflows of one cycle.

fields.name: status
fields.description: Only one cycle may be active per game; closing is an explicit operator action.

fields.name: original_baseline_revision
fields.description: Source revision captured at cycle opening. Immutable.

fields.name: head_revision
fields.description: Canonical cycle head. Only epoch integrations and remote-application boundaries advance it.

fields.name: timeline
fields.description: Ordered head-lineage record. Head-advancing entries are transactional with their commits; save points are evidence anchors pinned to existing commits. See the timeline entry-kind table below.

fields.name: workflow_ids
fields.description: Child run, PR, and sync workflows in creation order.

props.name: CycleState

text.insert: Baseline and Head
Each cycle captures one immutable baseline and advances one head_revision. Recovery reads those durable fields instead of inferring current source truth from workflow logs or dashboard history.

rows: Opening baseline
The source revision and game policy captured at open never change.
Later configuration edits cannot rewrite the meaning of existing work.
head_revision
The canonical commit currently owned by the active cycle.
The canonical worktree must agree with it at durable boundaries.
Head lineage
Only accepted Run integration and source-changing sync publication advance head.
PR phases and save points add evidence without pretending source moved.
Successor baseline
A new cycle captures a fresh baseline only after its predecessor closes.
Two cycles never compete for future head lineage.

text.insert: Open a Cycle
Opening turns the worktree prepared by
Registration and Setup
into an active cycle only after its source boundary is complete and verified. The
Sync Workflow
performs Baseline Preparation when source reconciliation is required.

steps.text: Require every prior cycle for the game to be closed
Allocate the envelope and capture baseline preparation outside the active slot
Provision or identify the canonical worktree
Run opening sync when source preparation is required
Verify the worktree, baseline, and opening head name the same source boundary
Install active CycleState and append `cycle.opened` in one durable boundary

text.insert: The first cycle has no predecessor head. Provisioning plus opening sync establishes its baseline; bootstrap may omit opening_sync_id only when provisioning itself supplies the validated source boundary. No active CycleState is exposed with an incomplete baseline or missing worktree identity.
Single Active Cycle

A game has at most one cycle in active or closing ownership. Historical closed cycles remain readable, an active cycle persists while dispatch authority is free, and no workflow transition opens or closes a cycle automatically.
Ordered Timeline
The timeline records head lineage and workflow evidence in one durable order. Each entry kind has one writer, one head effect, and a failure rule that keeps recovery deterministic.

rows: Run integrator
Record one confirmed epoch integration commit.
Advances head_revision.
The entry exists if and only if the integration commit exists.
Sync publisher
Record confirmed source reconciliation and its prior/new heads.
Advances head_revision for source-changing sync only.
The entry, repoint, invalidations, and accepted publication commit as one recoverable boundary.
PR campaign
Record campaign activation and release evidence.
No head change.
Lease-bound campaign evidence must settle before authority releases.
Save-point capture
Pin reports, board state, and score evidence to an existing commit.
No head change.
Capture failure marks evidence stale and blocks the cycle without inventing or reverting a commit.

text.insert: Workflow Authority
A cycle retains sync, run, and PR state at the same time, while
Harness State
owns the one-active-workflow-slot invariant. Moving authority changes which child may act; it does not replace the cycle or discard inactive state.

rows: Run
Acquires dispatch authority for scheduling, workers, and integration.
Confirmed epoch integration appends epoch_completed and advances head.
A managed stop settles active work before release.
PR
Acquires authority for bounded campaign preparation, review, and repair.
pr_phase evidence is appended without changing head.
Campaign activation settles and releases without closing the cycle.
Sync
An observed request waits until the current owner stops and releases; staging remains isolated.
Confirmed source publication appends remote_application and may advance head.
Publication, cancellation, or recovery settles staging before release.
Knowledge
Uses jobs-table leases, never the game dispatch lease.
Accepted knowledge may advance its own revision but never cycle head.
Job lease settlement is independent of workflow handoff.

text.insert: Close Explicitly

steps.text: Require the game dispatch lease to be free
Verify the canonical worktree contains no changes beyond `head_revision`
Require fresh evidence and a named save point whose commit equals head
Record the final evidence boundary and transition to `closed`
Clear the current HarnessState cycle slot
No workflow transition closes the cycle automatically
